import Snippet from "../../../../components/docs/Snippet.astro";

The Kotlin drop-in reads the device's license document from the `X-PKey-License` header, verifies it offline against your pinned keys and refuses the request when the license doesn't allow it. A route with no gate stays open. The contract is on [Verify licenses on your server](/docs/build/servers/).

Requires the License feature and the config file `pkey sdk --lang kotlin --write` writes. The app sends `X-PKey-License` and `X-PKey-Device` with each call to your server.

## Steps

1. **Server** Add `im.plrs.key:polaris-key-server-ktor` from Polaris Key's Maven feed, and generate `PolarisConfig.kt` with `pkey sdk --lang kotlin --write`.
2. **Server** Install the provider once, in `install(Authentication)`.
3. **Server** Wrap each route that needs a gate: `requireLicense`, `requireEntitlement`, `requireTier`, `requireSignIn` or `requireAll`.

<Snippet
  src="packages/shared-manifest/test/fixtures/integration/kotlin/server/licensing.ktor.kt"
  title="Application.kt"
/>

`polarisKey` never refuses. Only the `require*` blocks do. `call.requirePolarisLicense()` returns the license without a null check, and throws if the route has no gate; `call.polarisLicense` is the nullable form. A missing, empty or malformed product fails at startup with a message that names the fix.

## Require a signed-in account

`requireSignIn` refuses with `sign_in_required` (403) while no account is signed in on the device. Wrap the route the same way as `requireEntitlement`.
